# Overview

This is the second page of a three-page workflow examining
**moment-to-moment dyadic dynamics in baseline couple interaction warmth**.
It begins with the validated wide-format baseline warmth dataset created on the
[Import & Reliability](Import_BL_WH_Syntax_annotated_v4.qmd) page and prepares the second-by-second
trajectories used in the synchrony analysis.

The processing workflow:

1. reshapes the wide SPSS file from one row per couple with one column per
   second into one row per couple-second;
2. recodes the missing-value placeholder to `NA`;
3. creates separate positive- and negative-discussion person-level long
   datasets for mom and partner;
4. saves the three analysis ready long files used by the synchrony calculation;
   and
5. plots warmth trajectories for the full sample and a representative subset
   as a visual data-quality and interpretive check.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
### Workflow

**1. Import & Reliability** → **2. Processing & Visualization** → **3. Synchrony Calculation**

[Import & Reliability](Import_BL_WH_Syntax_annotated_v4.qmd) · [Processing & Visualization](Baseline-Synchrony_Processing.qmd) · [Synchrony Calculation](Baseline-Synchrony_Calculation.qmd)
:::


The preceding page documents the original CARMA import, validation, and
reliability workflow: [Import & Reliability](Import_BL_WH_Syntax_annotated_v4.qmd). The next page
uses the processed long-format files to calculate concurrent and time-lagged
synchrony: [Synchrony Calculation](Baseline-Synchrony_Calculation.qmd).

# Data Cleaning

**Load Packages**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Load packages used for reshaping, visualization, time-series analysis, modeling, and formatted output
library(here)
library(nlme)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2) 
library(lavaan)
library(semTools)
library(jtools)
library(haven)
library(modsem)
library(forecast)
library(gt)
```
:::






## Transformation

The raw file has one row per couple and separate columns for each second
of the interaction (e.g. `blmnwh.6`, `blmnwh.7`, ...). This section
reshapes that into a single long-format table (one row per
couple-second), recodes the dataset's missing-value placeholder to `NA`,
and then splits the negative- and positive-discussion variables into
their own person-level long datasets for plotting and later synchrony
calculation.

**Reshape Wide to Long**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Transform data wide to long
BL_WH_WidetoLong <- BL_WH %>%
  pivot_longer(
    # Select columns like blmnwh.6, blmnwh.7, etc
    cols = matches("^[^.]+\\.\\d+$"), 
    
    # Split variable name based on period
    names_to = c(".value", "second"),  
    names_sep = "\\." ) %>%
  
  # Convert second to numeric
  mutate(second = as.numeric(second))
```
:::





**Recode Missing Values**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Select the four warmth variables, second, ID
BL_WH_Long <- BL_WH_WidetoLong %>%
  select(ID, second, blmnwh, blmpwh, blfnwh, blfpwh)

# Set 0 as missing
BL_WH_Long$blmnwh[BL_WH_Long$blmnwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blmpwh[BL_WH_Long$blmpwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blfnwh[BL_WH_Long$blfnwh == 0] <- NA
BL_WH_Long$blfpwh[BL_WH_Long$blfpwh == 0] <- NA
```
:::

**Create Negative Interaction Dataset**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create long format for negative interaction
# (Blmnwh = mom, blfnwh = partner)

BL_WH_Neg_Long <- BL_WH_Long %>%
  select(ID, second, blmnwh, blfnwh) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(blmnwh, blfnwh),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "blnwh") %>%
  mutate(
    personF = case_when(
      source == "blmnwh" ~ "mom",  # Mom
      source == "blfnwh" ~ "partner" ),  # Partner
    personN = case_when(
      source == "blmnwh" ~ 1,  # Mom
      source == "blfnwh" ~ 2 ))  # Partner

# Set personF as factor
BL_WH_Neg_Long$personF <- as.factor(BL_WH_Neg_Long$personF)

# Set personN as factor
BL_WH_Neg_Long$personN <- as.numeric(BL_WH_Neg_Long$personN)
```

## Panel Plots {#secPanel}

The two figures below show second-by-second warmth trends for the full
sample, split by person (mom vs. partner) and by discussion type
(negative vs. positive). The two figures after that repeat the same
comparison for a representative subset of couples, faceted individually,
so that couple-level variation around the sample trend is visible rather
than smoothed away.

**Warmth During Negative Discussion**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="figure code"}
# Plot all negative-discussion warmth trajectories to inspect dyad-level patterns and potential data anomalies
fig_blnegative_warmth <- ggplot(data = BL_WH_Neg_Long, aes(second, blnwh, color = personF)) +
  geom_smooth(linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("mom" = "#CC6677", "partner" = "#88CCEE"), name = "Person") +
  labs(title = "Couple Warmth During Negative Discussion") +
  xlab("Time") +
  ylab("Average Warmth") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16), axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```
:::
